bug_semantics: ZPan initialized its process-wide HS512 JWT helper with the public constant "123". A remote attacker who knows that repository-visible secret can sign a z-token whose subject and roles claim an administrator identity; LoginAuthWithRoles accepts the signature and then authorizes protected API routes from the attacker-controlled roles, bypassing password authentication.
flaw_origin: Commit 4fae6e2bdcab183ef59dd9f4055e2633ec2523f5 added the new user/token authentication subsystem. Its newly created internal/app/service/token.go made NewToken call jwtutil.Init("123") and used that same global helper to issue and verify RoleClaims; the same commit added the cookie-to-roles authentication middleware and protected-route role checks. The hard-coded signing key, rather than a per-installation secret, is therefore part of the original implementation of this authentication mechanism, not a later move or refactor of pre-existing vulnerable lines.
ai_marker: absent: the raw BIC commit object for 4fae6e2bdcab183ef59dd9f4055e2633ec2523f5 names human author and committer saltbo <saltbo@foxmail.com>, contains only the subject "refactor: remove the moreu depend && add user supports", and has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, or bot trailer/identity.
evidence: First-party issue https://github.com/saltbo/zpan/issues/219 identifies internal/app/service/token.go:16, HS512 key "123", and demonstrates a forged administrator z-token against a protected system-options endpoint; the maintainer links PR #410, commit 8662db8d4b06057631faf3deba4132e66705e947, and release v1.6.6 as the fix. `git log -L '/func NewToken()/,+5':internal/app/service/token.go 8662db8d4b06057631faf3deba4132e66705e947^` traces `jwtutil.Init("123")` to 4fae6e2bdcab183ef59dd9f4055e2633ec2523f5. An all-history `git log -S 'jwtutil.Init("123")' --pickaxe-all --find-renames -- '*.go'` finds that addition, the later v2 reset removal, and the v1 security fix, with no earlier writer. Direct diff 3de132e2248fa8257f5e0dc2aa688bff8f94418c..4fae6e2bdcab183ef59dd9f4055e2633ec2523f5 shows internal/app/service/token.go created from /dev/null with NewToken, Create, Verify, and RoleClaims; `git ls-tree` shows that path absent in the immediate parent, while `git grep` of the parent finds neither the exact hard-coded initializer nor an earlier equivalent user-token signing setup. `git tag --contains 4fae6e2bdcab183ef59dd9f4055e2633ec2523f5` begins at v1.5.0 (v1.4.1 predates the BIC) and includes v1.6.5 and v1.7.0-beta2. Tag-tree greps confirm the exact hard-coded initializer in v1.5.0, v1.6.5, and v1.7.0-beta2. The advisory package range is <1.6.6 with first patched version 1.6.6; tag v1.6.6 points exactly to 8662db8d4b06057631faf3deba4132e66705e947, whose sole parent is the v1.6.5 commit 33eec01e971f206356c76df79c4148e3f8d1752f. Its direct diff replaces `jwtutil.Init("123")` with `jwtutil.Init(JWTSecret())`, generates 32 random bytes, persists `security.jwt_secret` for new and upgraded installations, and uses that configured key for share-token issue/verification as well. `git cat-file -p 4fae6e2bdcab183ef59dd9f4055e2633ec2523f5` supplies the BIC-only authorship/trailer evidence used for attribution.
reasoning: The vulnerability is exploitable because HS512 is symmetric: knowledge of the constant signing key is enough to mint a structurally valid token with arbitrary administrator roles, and the middleware derives authorization from claims after verifying them with that same constant. History analysis chooses 4fae6e2bdcab183ef59dd9f4055e2633ec2523f5 rather than a later release, reset, or fix because it is the first commit to write both the exact weak-key initializer and the new authentication path that consumes attacker-forgeable role claims. Although its subject says refactor and the commit moves many unrelated files, token.go and the user-token authentication mechanism are new additions; exact-string pickaxe and line history expose no earlier vulnerable source to follow, so there is no smaller prior BIC to decompose. The immediate parent tree lacks both token.go and the hard-coded initializer, establishing parent absence. The BIC is included from v1.5.0 onward, the constant remains in the reported v1.6.5 and v1.7.0-beta2 trees, and the v1.6.6 tag is the direct fixing commit on top of v1.6.5, satisfying the affected/patched boundary. Finally, attribution is based only on the raw BIC commit object: it records a human author/committer and no AI marker. Under the protocol, the closed verdict is therefore NOT_AI.
